input.quote: Under no circumstances shall any Party be liable to any other Party in contract, tort, (including negligence or breach of statutory duty) or otherwise for loss (whether direct or indirect) of profits, property, traffic, business or anticipated savings, or for any indirect or consequential loss or damage in connection with the operation of this Agreement howsoever caused.
input.rationale: The liability regime sits at the fallback on its material terms, so we do not redline it. (1) Mutuality: Paragraph 21.3 (p0242-p0245) binds "any Party" in favour of "any other Party" — the exclusion of indirect/consequential loss, lost profits, property, traffic, business and anticipated savings (expressly covering delay, damage to or failure of APCN 2 and service interruption) applies symmetrically to Teleglobe USA and every other APCN 2 Party, so there is no one-sided protection and no walk-away asymmetry. (2) Carve-outs: this is a multilateral consortium C&MA with no aggregate monetary cap anywhere in the document (confirmed by searches for cap/aggregate/limited-to-the-amount/liability and review of Paragraphs 4.9, 21, 23, 31, 32). Because no cap exists, liability for indemnification obligations (21.2, p0241), breach of the Paragraph 31 confidentiality covenant, gross negligence and wilful misconduct is already uncapped, so those four fallback elements are met by the structure rather than by express carve-out wording. (3) The only element short of the checklist is a stated mutual cap "based on 12 months of fees": there is no vendor/customer fee stream here (costs are APCN 2 Capital Costs and O&M Costs allocated under Schedule B), so a fees-based cap has nothing to attach to. In its place Teleglobe has two meaningful and mutual limitations — liability is "several and not joint or collective" (21.1, p0240), and third-party claims, indemnities and post-termination liabilities are confined to each Party's Schedule B proportion (21.2, 32.1, 32.5, 32.6). Noted for the file rather than flagged: no USD 1,000,000 floor, no "fees paid or payable" basis, no express Excluded Claims list and no statement that payment obligations fall outside the cap — all preferred-only mechanics. We would not press to insert an aggregate cap, as capping liability in this symmetric regime would limit the other Parties' exposure to us as much as ours to them.
